content:
Samir Patel: heads up — saw a cascade when primary model-pool hit capacity during the batch job spike. Clients got intermittent 502s then a pile of fallbacks to heavier models which made things worse.
Jill Nguyen: ugh. spike when? any tenant affinity or header hints in requests? :thinking_face:
Samir Patel: around 09:14 UTC. requests had `x-tenant-id` + some `x-routing-hint: low-latency`. Gateway routed to primary lane, pool saturated, CB opened, but fallback order picked a larger model with no quota check.
Matt O'Connell: can you paste a small trace? need to see the decision path.
Samir Patel: pasted excerpt from gateway trace: 
```
route.match: /v1/generate
policy: primary-lane
cb: triggered @95% util
fallbackChain: [largest-opt, regional-same-arch, cached-prefix]
selected: largest-opt (no tenant-quota check)
```
Priya Rao: that fallbackChain order is the problem — it doesn't consider tenant quota or soft-degrade preference. we should prefer a cheaper quantized variant or a cached prefix response before escalating.
Jill Nguyen: agreed. proposal: compute a dynamic fallback score per candidate: score = base_cost * (1 + penalty_if_over_quota) * latency_bias. prefer lower score. also allow tenant-specified `x-rw-fallback-preference` to nudge ordering.
Matt O'Connell: +1 but we must be careful with header precedence. tenants can override only within allowed guardrails. default deny if tenant tries to pick unverified model.
Samir Patel: rough config prototype: 
```
"fallbackPolicy": {
  "probe_order": ["cached_prefix","quantized_variant","regional_compatible"],
  "score_formula": "cost * (1 + over_quota_penalty) * latency_factor",
  "tenant_override_header": "x-rw-fallback-preference",
  "guardrails": ["verified_models_only","quota_check"]
}
```
ConsoleUX: from a rollout UX perspective, we should expose a per-route rollout editor that includes a "degrade profile" slider (aggressive <-> conservative). UI would show simulated latency/cost delta for each profile. non-admin tenants get read-only.
Priya Rao: telemetry ask: for every degraded response we need tags: `degrade_reason`, `selected_fallback`, `tenant_quota_state`, `cb_state`, and a small sample of request headers. these should map to Console traces and to alerts when degraded_rate > 1% per route.
Samir Patel: agreed. also want a short response shim option: instead of returning the heavier model output, we can return a 202 with `x-rw-degraded: true` + estimated ETA when result will be computed, and enqueue async. that helps bursty tenants.
Jill Nguyen: 202 shim is interesting but changes client expectations. need a feature flag and a clear SDK change log. we can default to in-protocol soft-degrade for internal clients only.
Matt O'Connell: circuit breaker tuning: open at 90% sustained for 30s, half-open probe interval 10s. fallback probe should do a lightweight token-generation request not a full decode to check real capacity.
Priya Rao: telemetry note: half-open probe results should be a separate metric `cb_probe_success` so we can correlate with degraded responses.
Samir Patel: i'll draft a PR for gateway policy + a small change to default fallbackChain to prefer `cached_prefix` and `quantized_variant` and add tenant guardrails.
deploy-bot: started CI pipeline for branch `samir/fallback-policy-tune` — build 1124 queued. :rocket:
Jill Nguyen: sweet. Samir, can you add a small migration for existing policies so old configs get a sane fallbackChain?
Samir Patel: yes. will include a safe migration that preserves explicit fallback orders but injects `quota_check: true` and adds `degrade_score` default for unspecified entries.
ConsoleUX: once PR lands, I'll add a console card that surfaces historical `degraded_rate` and the top 3 `selected_fallback` values per route. helps PMs decide if we need more capacity or better quantized models.
Matt O'Connell: one last ask: add a unit test that simulates tenant hitting quota and ensures fallback doesn't escalate to larger models. catches regressions.
Samir Patel: done. will ping when CI passes. thanks all. :thumbsup:
